_comment: Which model each tier resolves to when this profile is active. Every
component in this plugin asks for a TIER (model: sonnet, model: haiku)
and never for a model ID, so changing these four lines re-targets the
whole loop - no file in agents/ or skills/ mentions a provider.
VERIFY BEFORE USE: run `node profiles/check.js` to confirm each of these
IDs actually exists on OpenRouter right now. Model names are renamed and
retired constantly, and a stale ID here fails at the first request, in
the middle of a milestone, which is the worst possible moment to find
out. The values below are STARTING POINTS chosen for role, not
endorsements - check them, price them, and change them to suit.
Choosing per tier, by what the tier is used for here:
opus/fable - NOT only reached with --model opus: Claude Code's own built-in
Explore and Plan agents ask for them. In a real fallback session three
Explore agents on anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 ($3/$15) cost more than the
whole qwen3-coder main session. So they map to qwen3-coder too; spec, ADR and
roadmap work waits for the subscription window anyway.
coding (sonnet) - devkit-implementer and most subagents. Needs real
tool-use and long-context reliability; a model that cannot follow a
red-green loop will cost you more in reviewer rounds than it saves.
cheap (haiku) - devkit-reviewer, devkit-dep-audit, and background
work. Highest volume, lowest stakes, best place to save money.
maxContextTokens: Claude Code compacts the conversation as it nears this, so it
caps what each late request costs - every request re-sends the whole context,
and one long fallback session once spent about $8.50 that way. Lower is cheaper
but summarises older detail sooner. Your own CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS wins.
